body:
`root/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/cwa-auto-library/run` ends:

    python3 .../auto_library.py
    exit_code=$?
    if [[ ${exit_code} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "...completed successfully!"
    else echo "...did not complete successfully (exit code: ${exit_code})..."; fi

The `if` is the last statement, so the script's own status is the echo's -- always
0. Every `sys.exit(1)` in `auto_library.py` (there are four: two in
`set_library_location`/`update_calibre_web_db`, one in `update_dirs_json`, and the
"no usable library" stop added in #1429) is therefore invisible to s6. The
oneshot reports success and boot continues with an unconfigured or wrongly
configured library, which then fails later and further from the cause.

Noted while tracing #1429's blast radius, deliberately not changed there: it
touches every boot path and deserves its own change. Decide first whether a
failed auto-library SHOULD block boot -- swallowing may have been intentional so
a library problem does not make the container unstartable. If so, the fix is to
say so in a comment and keep the log line; if not, propagate the code.
title: cwa-auto-library swallows its own exit code, so a failed boot step reads as success
